article.body_html:
If you want to buy a used motorbike in Hanoi as a foreigner, the short answer is that the bike can only be put in your name if you hold a Vietnamese permanent or temporary residence card with at least six months left on it, the seller must first have the old registration revoked, and you then register the bike at the Hanoi Traffic Police Division, paying a registration tax of 1 per cent of the official valuation plus a plate-and-certificate fee. Renting for the same period involves none of those steps: the bike stays registered to the shop, and you only need the licence, passport and contract that any rental requires. This guide walks through the legal steps, the documents and the fees as published by the Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Finance, and then sets them against renting so you can decide which route fits your stay.

Who can register a used motorbike in Vietnam

Vehicle registration in Vietnam is governed by Circular 79/2024/TT-BCA of the Ministry of Public Security, in force since 1 January 2025 and amended twice in 2025. The consolidated text published on the Government portal sets out, in Article 10, what papers an owner must present. A Vietnamese citizen uses a level-2 electronic identification account or shows a citizen ID card or passport. A foreign owner who lives and works in Vietnam must show a permanent residence card or a temporary residence card that still has at least six months of validity. Diplomatic and consular staff follow a separate route through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

That single rule decides most cases. A visitor on a tourist visa or an e-visa does not hold a residence card, so the registration office has no document to accept, and the bike cannot be put in that visitor's name. The same consolidated circular adds, in Article 35, that a registration certificate issued to a foreigner living and working in Vietnam carries the expiry date of the residence card, so ownership is tied to the length of your permitted stay rather than being open-ended. Article 3 also says that an owner registers in the locality where they have their permanent or temporary residence registration, which for most expatriates in the capital means Hanoi.

Where you file matters too. Under Article 4 of the same text, commune-level police register motorbikes for domestic organisations and individuals, while the provincial Traffic Police Division (Phòng Cảnh sát giao thông) handles vehicles of anyone resident in the province that are not covered by the national-level list. The Ministry of Public Security's public-service summary of Circular 79/2024 states this directly: motorbikes of foreign organisations and individuals are registered at the Traffic Police Division, not at the ward police station that a Vietnamese neighbour might use.

Ownership transfer step by step

Buying second-hand is legally a change of owner, which the circular calls registering a transfer of name (đăng ký sang tên). It is a two-part procedure, and the seller's part comes first.

Step 1: the seller has the old registration revoked

According to the Ministry of Public Security summary, when a vehicle is sold, gifted or inherited, the registered owner must keep the registration certificate and the number plate rather than hand them to the buyer, and must apply to the registration office for revocation within 30 days of signing the transfer document. If the seller misses the deadline or simply gives the papers to the buyer, the office opens an administrative penalty procedure before anything else is processed. The revocation file consists of a revocation declaration, the owner's identity papers, two rubbings of the engine and frame numbers, a copy of the transfer contract, and the certificate and plate. The consolidated circular's Article 7 gives the office two working days to issue the revocation certificate after a complete file, or eight working hours when the whole process is done online.

Two consequences follow for a buyer. First, insist on seeing the revocation certificate before paying in full, because without it the bike is still legally the seller's. Second, the plate on the bike will not stay with it: Article 3 of the consolidated text explains that plates are identity plates linked to the owner's personal identification number, and a foreigner's plate is linked to the foreigner identification number or residence card number. When ownership changes, the old plate is withdrawn and held for the seller for five years. You will receive a plate issued under your own identity.

Step 2: pay the registration tax

Before the buyer can register, the registration tax known as lệ phí trước bạ must be paid at the tax office. Article 13 of the consolidated circular lists the proof of payment among the documents of the registration file, either as electronic data received from the tax authority or as a paper receipt of payment into the state budget. The rate is set by the Government: the Government portal article on Decree 175/2025/NĐ-CP, effective 1 July 2025, quotes the amended Article 8 of Decree 10/2022: motorbikes pay 2 per cent, and a motorbike on which the tax is paid for the second time or later pays 1 per cent. A used bike that was properly registered once before therefore falls in the 1 per cent bracket. The same article notes that the tax base is the valuation table issued by the provincial People's Committee, not the price you agreed with the seller, so ask the tax office for the table figure for your exact model and year.

Step 3: register in your name

The buyer then files the registration half of the procedure. The Ministry of Public Security summary lists the file: a registration declaration, the owner's papers, the transfer document, the registration-tax receipt, and the revocation certificate obtained in Step 1. Article 17 of the consolidated circular adds that the buyer brings the bike to the office for a physical inspection of the engine and frame numbers against the declaration, receives an appointment slip, pays the registration fee and collects the plate, and then collects the certificate at the office or by postal delivery. Article 7 sets the time limit for the certificate at two working days from a complete file, with the plate issued on the spot once the file is accepted.

The public-service listing for first-time registration at commune police describes the same mechanics from the counter's side: the owner declares online and receives a queue number and appointment by SMS or email, the officer checks the identity data, the invoice, the tax receipt and the origin documents, compares the bike's brand, engine number, frame number and colour against the declaration, assigns a plate randomly from the system, and collects the fee before handing over the plate. The circular's summary also reminds owners that they need a bank account if they want to pay or receive refunds of the registration fee online.

Registration fee and plates in Hanoi from 2026

The fee for the certificate and plate is separate from the registration tax and is set by the Ministry of Finance. From 1 January 2026 it follows Circular 155/2025/TT-BTC, and the Government portal's summary of the fee schedule places Hanoi in Area I, covering every ward and commune of the city. For a motorbike receiving a new certificate and plate in Area I, the fee depends on the bike's official value: 700,000 VND for a bike valued up to 15 million VND, 1,400,000 VND for a value above 15 million and up to 40 million, and 2,800,000 VND above 40 million. Replacing a certificate together with a plate for a motorbike costs 70,000 VND, replacing a certificate alone costs 35,000 VND, and replacing a motorbike plate costs 50,000 VND. The value used is the same registration-tax valuation at the time of registration.

Which line applies to a second-hand transfer depends on how the registration office classifies your case, because a transfer can involve a new identity plate for the buyer. Ask the officer to state the applicable line and the amount before you pay, and keep the receipt with the bike's papers. The schedule also lists exemptions, but these cover diplomatic missions, their accredited staff and three-wheeled motorbikes for disabled riders, not ordinary private buyers.

Buying versus renting for the same period

Set side by side, the two routes differ less in money than in paperwork and exposure.

  • Eligibility. Buying requires a residence card with six months remaining and a Hanoi residence registration. Renting requires a valid licence for the bike's class, identification and a contract; the bike remains registered to the shop, and the rental registration guide on matching the bike to its papers explains what to check on the shop's certificate at pickup.
  • Steps and deadlines. Buying involves the seller's revocation within 30 days, a tax-office visit, a physical inspection at the Traffic Police Division and two separate waits of up to two working days. Renting is a single handover.
  • Fees. Buying adds a 1 per cent registration tax on the official valuation plus the certificate-and-plate fee, with the main Area I tiers running from 700,000 VND to 2,800,000 VND. Renting is a flat rate per day, week or month; as a comparison point, reference prices at Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà for an automatic scooter by the month start from about 1,200,000 VND, and you should confirm the exact bike and rate before booking. The monthly rental rates page sets out the current brackets.
  • Exit. When you leave, a bike you own has to be sold again, which puts you in the seller's seat with the same 30-day revocation duty, and your certificate expires with your residence card. A rental simply goes back to the shop.
  • Risk if the paperwork is skipped. A bike bought on a handshake without the revocation and transfer stays registered to a stranger. The circular's summary is explicit that the person named on the certificate keeps the owner's legal responsibilities until revocation is completed.

For a stay of a few weeks or months, the arithmetic rarely favours buying once the tax, the fee, the time at three different offices and the resale are counted, and for anyone without a residence card the question does not arise. For a long-term resident with a work permit and a temporary residence card, ownership becomes realistic, and a shop that sells documented bikes can shorten the search; the Hanoi motorbike for sale page describes what fully documented means in practice. If you decide to rent instead, Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà is at Ngõ 5 Nguyễn Văn Cừ, Bồ Đề, Long Biên, Hà Nội, open 09:00 to 21:00 daily, hotline 0334 699 969.

Checklist before you hand over money for a used bike

  • Confirm your own residence card has at least six months left, as Article 10 of the consolidated circular requires.
  • Match the engine and frame numbers on the bike to the seller's registration certificate, and check the seller's name against their ID.
  • Sign a written transfer document; the seller needs a copy for the revocation file and you need it for the registration file.
  • Wait for the seller's revocation certificate before paying the balance.
  • Pay the registration tax at the tax office and keep the receipt or electronic record.
  • Book the Traffic Police Division appointment through the public-service portal, bring the bike, and budget for the Area I fee tier that matches the official valuation.
  • Make sure you hold a licence that covers the bike's engine size; the motorcycle licence rules guide covers what is accepted for foreign riders.

FAQ

Can a tourist on a visa buy and register a motorbike in Hanoi?

Not in their own name. Article 10 of the consolidated Circular 79/2024 text requires a foreign owner living and working in Vietnam to present a permanent or temporary residence card with at least six months remaining, and a tourist visa is neither. Renting is the lawful alternative for a short stay.

How much is the registration tax on a used motorbike?

Decree 175/2025/NĐ-CP sets the motorbike registration tax at 2 per cent, reduced to 1 per cent from the second payment onward, calculated on the provincial valuation table rather than the sale price. A previously registered used bike normally falls under the 1 per cent rate.

Does the number plate come with the bike?

No. Plates are identity plates tied to the owner. The seller's plate is withdrawn at revocation and held for them for five years, and you receive a plate issued under your own foreigner identification or residence card number.

How long does the transfer take?

Each half has its own limit under Article 7: two working days for the revocation certificate after a complete file, and two working days for the new registration certificate, with the plate issued when the file is accepted. The seller's 30-day deadline to start revocation runs from the date of the transfer document.

Where in Hanoi does a foreigner register a motorbike?

At the Hanoi Traffic Police Division. Commune and ward police register motorbikes only for domestic owners, as Article 4 of the consolidated circular and the Ministry of Public Security summary both state.
